p: The park hit the headlines in 2020 when a handful of newly arrived African grey parrots started swearing at visitors, and staff had to split them up to stop them teaching each other new words. It's a funny story, but it also shines a light on the serious side of the place: it takes in huge numbers of parrots that people can no longer keep. Walking among so many birds is a genuinely remarkable sight, and the noise is something else.

Allow plenty of time, because the site is bigger than many first-timers expect. Pace yourselves, take in the big cats, wander the bird areas and let the kids have a play when they need it. The flat paths make it accessible for wheelchairs and buggies, which is a real plus, and there's enough space for a picnic if the weather's fine. A thermos is worth packing on chilly days, as the open fens offer little shelter from the wind.

For a combined day on the coast, Skegness has plenty more to offer. Natureland Seal Sanctuary on the north end of the seafront rescues and cares for seals, and it's a lovely, smaller visit for animal fans. Up at Ingoldmells, Fantasy Island brings big rides and a huge market, and Skegness itself has the classic seafront with its clock tower, amusements and wide sands. Heading inland, Boston's Stump, the towering church of St Botolph, is a landmark you can see for miles across the flat fens, and Wainfleet, home of Batemans Brewery, is a characterful little market town on the way back towards Skegness.
